speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with yellowish discoloration of your skin; this is called jaundice. To determine the cause, how long has this yellowing been present, and have you noticed poor feeding or a fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiologic Jaundice)
Based on the history of a 5-day-old full-term infant with jaundice starting on day 3-4, normal stool and urine output, and exclusive breastfeeding, this is consistent with breastfeeding jaundice due to insufficient milk intake rather than pathologic causes. I recommend a Serum Bilirubin level to confirm the degree of jaundice. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Bilirubin_Total_and_Direct
